title: Cave Diving: Totally Nuts
summary: Josh and Chuck open with tour dates (Seattle, San Francisco Sketch Fest, Movie Crush live) and then cover cave diving: how it differs from open water and cavern diving, its fatality statistics, silt-outs, equipment (masks, fins, drysuits, redundant gear), gas mixtures (nitrox, heliox, trimix), decompression and the rule of thirds, guideline and Dorf markers, famous cave systems and archaeology, the 2018 Thailand cave rescue, and certification. The episode closes with listener mail about a listener who quit over a conversion therapy episode and a reply from listener Jordan.

entities.name: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood

segments.title: Tour announcements
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck announce tour dates in Seattle, San Francisco Sketch Fest at the Castro Theater on January 10, and Movie Crush live.

segments.title: Opening banter and caving anecdotes
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the episode with personal diving and caving stories, including a fatal caving incident and Chuck's experience lunking.

segments.title: Cave diving vs. open water and cavern diving
segments.summary: The hosts define cavern diving (daylight visible, within about 130 linear feet of the cave mouth, under 70 feet deep) and cave diving (overhead environment with no direct vertical access to the surface). They discuss the dangers and the motivation of exploration.

segments.title: Cave diving fatalities and silt-outs
segments.summary: The hosts cite a study of thirty years of American cave diving fatalities (161 divers, 67 trained and 87 untrained), with most deaths in Florida from running out of gas after silt-outs. They discuss panic and early cave diving deaths.

segments.title: Diving equipment and kick technique
segments.summary: The hosts cover masks, fins, and frog kicks used to avoid stirring silt and damaging formations, buoyancy control, the pull-and-glide technique, and spring versus sump caves.

segments.title: Drysuits, redundancy and gear
segments.summary: The hosts discuss wet suits versus dry suits, carrying redundant lights and knives, and keeping gear streamlined to avoid tangles.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Short break before the next topic.

segments.title: Breathing gases, decompression and the rule of thirds
segments.summary: The hosts explain decompression, the bends, nitrogen narcosis, and oxygen toxicity. They cover nitrox, heliox, and trimix, and the rule of thirds for gas use on the way out.

segments.title: Guidelines, Dorf markers and the cave dive scooter
segments.summary: The hosts describe guidelines, the entry line, and Dorf markers, which were invented by Lewis Holzendorf and improved by Forrest Wilson. They also discuss DPVs (diver propulsion vehicles).

segments.title: Famous cave systems, archaeology and the Thailand rescue
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the longest and deepest flooded caves, the Hoyo Negro remains, underwater archaeology, certification steps, and the 2018 Thailand cave rescue of a soccer team.
